key_drivers: New Section 301 tariffs (10-12.5%) on EU/Japan/Korea/Taiwan hit ENTG's imported specialty chemicals and materials directly; a Q3 guide has to absorb them
Persistent negative reaction base rate: 6 of last 8 prints down, median -5.6%, worst -14.6%
Q1 guide already pointed EPS down sequentially ($0.76-0.84 vs $0.86 delivered) on flat-to-up sales; margin story deteriorating
Preview notes ENTG has missed revenue estimates multiple times over two years; group down 12.7% in a month, ENTG down 18.1%
Offset: washed-out positioning ($166 avg PT vs ~$120 spot) and blowout peer prints (FormFactor +26%, Teradyne) leave real bounce risk
what_would_change_my_mind: A Q3 guide above the $845m Q2 top end with tariff costs explicitly absorbed and no gross-margin cut would likely produce a violent relief rally instead.
reasoning: ENTG is the laggard of a red-hot sector: peers up triple digits YTD, ENTG +39% and -18% in the last month. Fresh Section 301 tariffs on exactly its import geographies land two weeks before the print and must be reflected in guidance. Its guide-down habit and 6-of-8 negative reaction record compound that. Against it: sentiment and price are already washed out and peers are beating hard, so the distribution is wide and two-tailed. Modest short tilt, big expected move given 76% realised vol.

key_drivers: Middle East conflict independently flagged as a live travel drag (Expedia lost ~2pts of bookings growth to it); BKNG is the most EMEA-exposed OTA
Consensus already cut hard: Q2 revenue growth expected 5.7% vs 16.2% last quarter, so the bar is low and BKNG habitually beats
Stock up 6.5% in a month while consumer internet fell 4.2% - the run-in is spent
Tape is punishing beats in the group: Alphabet -7.1% and Reddit -21.8% post-print despite topping estimates
Small historical reactions (median 2.37%), 4 up / 4 down, no directional base rate
what_would_change_my_mind: A room-nights and gross-bookings beat with an explicitly unaffected Q3 outlook would flip this up, since the low revenue bar leaves plenty of room.
reasoning: Two forces cancel. The bar is unusually low (5.7% growth expected) and BKNG has a strong beat record, which argues up. But the stock outperformed its group into the print, the Middle East war is a confirmed drag on international travel across three separate corpus documents, and the current tape sold Alphabet 7% on a beat. Historical reactions are small and evenly split. No edge; size the move above the 2.37% median because realised vol is running well above BKNG's norm.

key_drivers: Clinical-stage biotech: Q2 report is cash runway plus timelines, not a numbers event, unless a pipeline disclosure rides along
Last real catalyst (CAPTIVATE Phase 3 CIDP interim responder data) was already disclosed on 2026-06-12, so the near-term news is spent
Stock at its 52-week high, +488% off the low, +15.3% in 20d and +8.65% in 5d into a routine quarterly - momentum with nothing specific behind it
Financing risk: a Phase 3 name at highs is a natural candidate to pair earnings with a raise
Corpus is essentially empty - zero news kept, zero StockTwits, zero HN - so any directional view is unsupported
what_would_change_my_mind: Any new claseprubart data or a registrational timeline pulled forward in the release would dominate the print and take it sharply up.
reasoning: Nothing in this corpus carries a bar. The June corporate-presentation 8-K shows the interim CIDP data is already public, so the August quarterly should be a financial-plus-timelines release. Prior reactions split evenly and the large ones (+21.5%, +8.0%) coincided with data, not with routine quarters. A hot 5-day run into a non-catalyst plus dilution risk at 52-week highs gives a whisker of downside skew, no more. Low certainty; the evidence layer is basically absent.

key_drivers: Reaction base rate is mildly positive: 6 of last 8 up, average +1.14%, and no move beyond 3.4% in two years
Sold off 4.2% in five sessions into the print - about 1.5 sigma for a 19% realised-vol utility, so some de-risking has already happened
Q2 is the seasonally trivial quarter for a gas LDC; the release is a FY guidance reaffirm more than an earnings event
Peer read-across is mixed but benign: NFG beat EPS by 4.8% while missing on revenue, and utility fundamentals are stable
Valuation is stretched (17.8x vs ~14x peers, ~11% premium to DDM), which caps upside
what_would_change_my_mind: A cut or narrowing to the low end of full-year EPS guidance, or an equity-issuance announcement to fund capex, would turn this negative.
reasoning: A regulated LDC reporting its smallest quarter, with an intact positive reaction base rate and a five-day pullback into the event. The only bearish input is valuation, which is a slow argument rather than an event-day one. Expect a small move close to the 1.75% historical median with a modest upward tilt from the reaffirm-and-bounce pattern. Evidence is thin - one valuation piece and one peer print - so conviction on direction stays low even though the move size is confidently small.

key_drivers: Q2 net sales already pre-announced on 2026-07-22 ($341m, +2% y/y) - the top line is fully de-risked and the market has already paid for it
Stock sits exactly at its 52-week high and above the $125.80 average analyst target, at 24.8x forward P/E on ~2% growth
What is left to learn is margin and the full-year guide, and last quarter delivered a significant gross-margin miss
Middle East war a confirmed 3% headwind in Q2; European operations down 4% with Lacoste -19% and Eastern Europe soft
Aug 5 11:00 ET call falls inside the close-to-close window, so guidance tone gets priced within the measurement period
what_would_change_my_mind: A gross-margin recovery plus a raised full-year EPS outlook would justify the 52-week-high price and send it up instead.
reasoning: The July 22 sales pre-announcement is decisive: revenue cannot surprise, so the print reduces to margin and guidance, and margin is exactly where IPAR disappointed last quarter. The stock has already rallied to its 52-week high and past the consensus target on that known-good sales number, leaving the risk one-sided. Pre-announced revenue also compresses move size, so I expect something near the 1.95% median, slightly wider because the guide and the next-morning call both land in the window.
